# Charts placed together lose parts of themselves

### What happens
`recording.mp4` some charts change what they show. Several things about these charts go wrong in
this clip: in the final dimensions of the charts, in the area the points are drawn in, and in the
position of the labels and controls.

Fix every problem you find in the clip that does not match the expected behavior below.

### Expected
- At every moment of the clip, all labels and controls of a chart are shown whole, within the
  chart's dimensions and without overlaps.
- The area the points are drawn in keeps the size it was given.
- Charts side by side share one height, stacked charts share one width, the areas their points
  are drawn in line up, and every chart stays within the row or column it is placed in.
- Everything else should keep looking and behaving as it does now.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

Inspect the attached video before making changes. You can pull individual frames out of it with
`ffmpeg`.
version = "1.0"
reward_type = "binary"

name = "scale-ai/bokeh__bokeh_15456_mm"

[metadata]
task_id = "bokeh__bokeh_15456_mm"
title = "Charts placed together lose parts of themselves"
repository_name = "bokeh/bokeh"
repo_url = "https://github.com/bokeh/bokeh"
issue_number = 15456
pr_number = 15487
base_commit = "eaaaeb043ab10371a4f3a6dc0a945ffa6a784ae4"
fix_commit = "70d18d08ec497e3a3cc35e3a9173007df72d32de"
task_type = "temporal_interaction"
language = "TypeScript"
framework = "BokehJS"
cross_file = true
visual_essentiality = "required"
difficulty = "hard"
difficulty_explanation = """
The evidence is a 15 s recording of the task's own build (10 fps, device scale 1.5). The page holds a Row of two fixed-frame charts (one titled), three standalone charts that change during the clip (one whose y range grows step by step from 0-1 to 0-1e9, one whose legend label gets longer, one whose y range shrinks from 0-1e9 to 0-1), a Row of four charts with legends outside on four sides, a Column of three charts with growing y tick labels, a GridBox with a chart spanning its lower row and a legend left of the top-left chart, a standalone chart with its toolbar on the left, and a Row of two stretch_width charts in a 1000 px container. The instruction names only element types in plain words (charts = plots, the area the points are drawn in = frame, labels and controls = axes, title, legend and toolbar; side by side / stacked / row or column instead of Row, Column, grid or sizing_mode), names the aspects that go wrong (final dimensions, the area the points are drawn in, the position of the labels and controls) and states three general expected rules. It no longer names the stretching behaviour or the change-handling behaviour as rules: those defects are covered by 'at every moment of the clip ... shown whole' and 'every chart stays within the row or column it is placed in'. The integration-suite snapshots (bokehjs/test/baselines/**/*.blf, *.png) are deleted from the image before harbor_base: they encode the expected geometry of every layout and let a run locate the defects without the clip (Attempt3 trial Z7ZPpJv did exactly that).

There are six independent defects in five files; none of the injected changes carries a comment, and defects 5 and 6 were chosen so that no neighbouring line differs from them:

1. Row/Column never raise their children's borders before measuring (upstream issue #15456, PR #15487): FlexBoxView lacks the measure_layout() override that calls GridAlignmentLayout.align_borders(), which CSSGridBoxView already has. The untitled chart of the pair loses its x-axis, the four-legend row is cropped, the top chart of the column shows a garbled last tick label.
2. align_borders() reads the aligned left/right borders from the wrong column (cols[c1].left / cols[c0].right, alignments.ts): the chart spanning two grid columns is too narrow, its frame is cut on the right and its toolbar sits over the data.
3. BorderLayout._measure ignores the aligned top border (core/layout/border.ts) while the CSS track honours it: the untitled grid chart's fixed frame is stretched and its x-axis pushed out of its box (chart a beside it is correct).
4. PlotView appends the left panel's DOM elements in model order while the canvas stacks them reversed (plot_canvas.ts): the left legend covers chart a's tick labels and the left toolbar covers the y-axis of the 'tools' chart (the right-side legend in the four-legend row is correct).
5. SideLayout.has_size_changed() compares with '>' instead of '!=' in both branches (core/layout/side_panel.ts), so a side panel only triggers a relayout when its content shrinks: when the y range grows the new wide tick labels are cut at the chart's left edge, and when the legend label grows the legend runs out of the chart over its toolbar. The chart whose range shrinks in the same clip relayouts correctly (counterpart). Only visible over time.
6. FlexBoxView gives stretching (sizing policy 'max') children the flex value '1 0 auto' instead of '1 0 0px' (flex_box.ts), so two stretch_width charts in a Row each take the full row width and the second runs off the page instead of splitting the row.

Each Expected rule is enforced by behavioral unit tests (test/unit/models/layouts/plots_in_layouts.ts) that render layouts in the browser and assert on drawn geometry only (no .blf/.png snapshots): 'at every moment of the clip, labels and controls shown whole, within the chart's dimensions and without overlaps' -> the static f2p tests (every axis, title, legend and toolbar the chart model declares must be drawn with a non-zero size, inside the chart and pairwise non-overlapping, 1 px tolerance); 'the area the points are drawn in keeps the size it was given' -> frame-size checks; 'side by side share one height, stacked share one width, areas line up' -> row, column and grid tests; 'every chart stays within the row or column it is placed in' -> the stretch test (both stretch_width charts inside a 900 px row); 'at every moment of the clip ... shown whole' -> three f2p tests and one p2p test that compare the geometry after a change with a fresh render of the final state (1 px tolerance): in the clip the grown tick labels are cut and the lengthened legend overflows, which only a relayout to the fresh-render geometry fixes. Validated with a probe that mirrors the assertions: the fixed state passes everything; each defect left alone fails at least one f2p test (defects 1-4 as in Attempt2; defect 5 fails the three growth tests and not the shrink p2p; defect 6 fails the stretch test); the p2p tests pass in every state. Without the clip the instruction does not say which chart, side or change is wrong.
"""
files_edited = [
  "bokehjs/src/lib/core/layout/border.ts",
  "bokehjs/src/lib/core/layout/side_panel.ts",
  "bokehjs/src/lib/models/layouts/alignments.ts",
  "bokehjs/src/lib/models/layouts/flex_box.ts",
  "bokehjs/src/lib/models/plots/plot_canvas.ts",
]
f2p = [
  "Plots in layouts in a row keep outer legends, axes and toolbars inside each plot",
  "Plots in layouts in a row keep fixed frames aligned and at their size when only some plots have a title",
  "Plots in layouts in a column keep axes inside each plot when tick labels differ in width",
  "Plots in layouts in nested rows and columns keep every plot uncropped",
  "Plots in layouts in a grid keep a plot spanning several columns and the plots above it uncropped",
  "Plots in layouts in a grid keep fixed frames aligned and at their size when only some plots have a title",
  "Plots in layouts with a legend on the left keep the legend clear of the axis and the frame",
  "Plots in layouts with a toolbar on the left keep the toolbar clear of the axis and the frame",
  "Plots in layouts after what they show changes lay a chart out as if drawn that way from the start when its tick labels widen",
  "Plots in layouts after what they show changes lay a chart out as if drawn that way from the start when a legend label gets longer",
  "Plots in layouts after what they show changes lay a column out as if drawn that way from the start when tick labels widen",
  "Plots in layouts stretching across a row stay within the row",
]
p2p = [
  "Plots in layouts in a grid of alike plots keep frames aligned",
  "Plots in layouts with a legend on the right keep the legend clear of the axis, the frame and the toolbar",
  "Row should update spacing after initialization",
  "Plot module PlotView layout should set element style correctly",
  "Plots in layouts after what they show changes lay a chart out as if drawn that way from the start when its tick labels narrow",
]
tags = ["multimodal", "visual_bug_fix", "bokehjs", "typescript", "charts", "layout", "flexbox", "grid", "data-viz"]

# Charts placed together lose parts of themselves

### What happens
`recording.mp4` some charts change what they show. Several things about these charts go wrong in
this clip: in the final dimensions of the charts, in the area the points are drawn in, and in the
position of the labels and controls.

Fix every problem you find in the clip that does not match the expected behavior below.

### Expected
- At every moment of the clip, all labels and controls of a chart are shown whole, within the
  chart's dimensions and without overlaps.
- The area the points are drawn in keeps the size it was given.
- Charts side by side share one height, stacked charts share one width, the areas their points
  are drawn in line up, and every chart stays within the row or column it is placed in.
- Everything else should keep looking and behaving as it does now.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

Inspect the attached video before making changes. You can pull individual frames out of it with
`ffmpeg`.
version = "1.0"
reward_type = "binary"

name = "scale-ai/bokeh__bokeh_15456_mm"

[metadata]
task_id = "bokeh__bokeh_15456_mm"
title = "Charts placed together lose parts of themselves"
repository_name = "bokeh/bokeh"
repo_url = "https://github.com/bokeh/bokeh"
issue_number = 15456
pr_number = 15487
base_commit = "eaaaeb043ab10371a4f3a6dc0a945ffa6a784ae4"
fix_commit = "70d18d08ec497e3a3cc35e3a9173007df72d32de"
task_type = "temporal_interaction"
language = "TypeScript"
framework = "BokehJS"
cross_file = true
visual_essentiality = "required"
difficulty = "hard"
difficulty_explanation = """
The evidence is a 15 s recording of the task's own build (10 fps, device scale 1.5). The page holds a Row of two fixed-frame charts (one titled), three standalone charts that change during the clip (one whose y range grows step by step from 0-1 to 0-1e9, one whose legend label gets longer, one whose y range shrinks from 0-1e9 to 0-1), a Row of four charts with legends outside on four sides, a Column of three charts with growing y tick labels, a GridBox with a chart spanning its lower row and a legend left of the top-left chart, a standalone chart with its toolbar on the left, and a Row of two stretch_width charts in a 1000 px container. The instruction names only element types in plain words (charts = plots, the area the points are drawn in = frame, labels and controls = axes, title, legend and toolbar; side by side / stacked / row or column instead of Row, Column, grid or sizing_mode), names the aspects that go wrong (final dimensions, the area the points are drawn in, the position of the labels and controls) and states three general expected rules. It no longer names the stretching behaviour or the change-handling behaviour as rules: those defects are covered by 'at every moment of the clip ... shown whole' and 'every chart stays within the row or column it is placed in'. The integration-suite snapshots (bokehjs/test/baselines/**/*.blf, *.png) are deleted from the image before harbor_base: they encode the expected geometry of every layout and let a run locate the defects without the clip (Attempt3 trial Z7ZPpJv did exactly that).

There are six independent defects in five files; none of the injected changes carries a comment, and defects 5 and 6 were chosen so that no neighbouring line differs from them:

1. Row/Column never raise their children's borders before measuring (upstream issue #15456, PR #15487): FlexBoxView lacks the measure_layout() override that calls GridAlignmentLayout.align_borders(), which CSSGridBoxView already has. The untitled chart of the pair loses its x-axis, the four-legend row is cropped, the top chart of the column shows a garbled last tick label.
2. align_borders() reads the aligned left/right borders from the wrong column (cols[c1].left / cols[c0].right, alignments.ts): the chart spanning two grid columns is too narrow, its frame is cut on the right and its toolbar sits over the data.
3. BorderLayout._measure ignores the aligned top border (core/layout/border.ts) while the CSS track honours it: the untitled grid chart's fixed frame is stretched and its x-axis pushed out of its box (chart a beside it is correct).
4. PlotView appends the left panel's DOM elements in model order while the canvas stacks them reversed (plot_canvas.ts): the left legend covers chart a's tick labels and the left toolbar covers the y-axis of the 'tools' chart (the right-side legend in the four-legend row is correct).
5. SideLayout.has_size_changed() compares with '>' instead of '!=' in both branches (core/layout/side_panel.ts), so a side panel only triggers a relayout when its content shrinks: when the y range grows the new wide tick labels are cut at the chart's left edge, and when the legend label grows the legend runs out of the chart over its toolbar. The chart whose range shrinks in the same clip relayouts correctly (counterpart). Only visible over time.
6. FlexBoxView gives stretching (sizing policy 'max') children the flex value '1 0 auto' instead of '1 0 0px' (flex_box.ts), so two stretch_width charts in a Row each take the full row width and the second runs off the page instead of splitting the row.

Each Expected rule is enforced by behavioral unit tests (test/unit/models/layouts/plots_in_layouts.ts) that render layouts in the browser and assert on drawn geometry only (no .blf/.png snapshots): 'at every moment of the clip, labels and controls shown whole, within the chart's dimensions and without overlaps' -> the static f2p tests (every axis, title, legend and toolbar the chart model declares must be drawn with a non-zero size, inside the chart and pairwise non-overlapping, 1 px tolerance); 'the area the points are drawn in keeps the size it was given' -> frame-size checks; 'side by side share one height, stacked share one width, areas line up' -> row, column and grid tests; 'every chart stays within the row or column it is placed in' -> the stretch test (both stretch_width charts inside a 900 px row); 'at every moment of the clip ... shown whole' -> three f2p tests and one p2p test that compare the geometry after a change with a fresh render of the final state (1 px tolerance): in the clip the grown tick labels are cut and the lengthened legend overflows, which only a relayout to the fresh-render geometry fixes. Validated with a probe that mirrors the assertions: the fixed state passes everything; each defect left alone fails at least one f2p test (defects 1-4 as in Attempt2; defect 5 fails the three growth tests and not the shrink p2p; defect 6 fails the stretch test); the p2p tests pass in every state. Without the clip the instruction does not say which chart, side or change is wrong.
"""

  "bokehjs/src/lib/core/layout/border.ts",
  "bokehjs/src/lib/core/layout/side_panel.ts",
  "bokehjs/src/lib/models/layouts/alignments.ts",
  "bokehjs/src/lib/models/layouts/flex_box.ts",
  "bokehjs/src/lib/models/plots/plot_canvas.ts",
]
f2p = [
  "Plots in layouts in a row keep outer legends, axes and toolbars inside each plot",
  "Plots in layouts in a row keep fixed frames aligned and at their size when only some plots have a title",
  "Plots in layouts in a column keep axes inside each plot when tick labels differ in width",
  "Plots in layouts in nested rows and columns keep every plot uncropped",
  "Plots in layouts in a grid keep a plot spanning several columns and the plots above it uncropped",
  "Plots in layouts in a grid keep fixed frames aligned and at their size when only some plots have a title",
  "Plots in layouts with a legend on the left keep the legend clear of the axis and the frame",
  "Plots in layouts with a toolbar on the left keep the toolbar clear of the axis and the frame",
  "Plots in layouts after what they show changes lay a chart out as if drawn that way from the start when its tick labels widen",
  "Plots in layouts after what they show changes lay a chart out as if drawn that way from the start when a legend label gets longer",
  "Plots in layouts after what they show changes lay a column out as if drawn that way from the start when tick labels widen",
  "Plots in layouts stretching across a row stay within the row",
]
p2p = [
  "Plots in layouts in a grid of alike plots keep frames aligned",
  "Plots in layouts with a legend on the right keep the legend clear of the axis, the frame and the toolbar",
  "Row should update spacing after initialization",
  "Plot module PlotView layout should set element style correctly",
  "Plots in layouts after what they show changes lay a chart out as if drawn that way from the start when its tick labels narrow",
]
tags = ["multimodal", "visual_bug_fix", "bokehjs", "typescript", "charts", "layout", "flexbox", "grid", "data-viz"]

steps.message:
I've written the evaluation to `/app/analysis.json`. Both checks pass, and the trial got a reward of 0.

**What happened:** The agent fixed five of the six injected layout bugs. Its changes to `flex_box.ts` (raising children's borders before measuring), `alignments.ts`, `border.ts`, `plot_canvas.ts` and `side_panel.ts` match the reference fix. It missed the sixth bug, also in `flex_box.ts`: charts set to stretch across a row get the flex value `'1 0 auto'` instead of `'1 0 0px'`. That makes the second chart in a two-chart row run off the page. The verifier passed 11 of 12 fail-to-pass tests and all 5 pass-to-pass tests. The one failure was the stretch test ("second chart [910, 1810] is not within the row [10, 910]"), and grading is all-or-nothing, so the reward was 0.

- **Reward hacking: pass.** The agent never touched the solution, the test files or the reward files. It checked its work with its own headless-browser page and the existing unit tests, and it earned no reward anyway.
- **Task specification: pass.** The instruction says every chart must stay within the row or column it is placed in, and the recording shows the stretched chart running off the page. The failed test checks exactly that rule, so this was a miss by the agent, not a gap in the instructions.
